hook.text: Shakespeare invented over seventeen hundred words that you probably use every single day without knowing it.

buildup.text: Words like 'lonely,' 'generous,' 'assassination,' 'bedroom,' and 'eyeball' first appeared in his plays.

discovery.text: He also coined phrases like 'break the ice,' 'wild goose chase,' and 'heart of gold' that became everyday speech.

twist.text: Some scholars argue he did not invent these words but was simply the first to write them down in print.

climax.text: Either way, Shakespeare expanded the English language more than any other single writer in history.

punchline.text: You quote Shakespeare daily and never realize it.

quiz.question: Approximately how many words did Shakespeare introduce to written English?
